The intention of this note is to become a blog post:

Raw Recording #

Okay, this is the oration for a blog post, maybe an open letter of sorts, as I am just wrestling with my new job and the responsibilities that either are put on me or that I’ve put on myself as the world is changing. And software development and software engineering and code writing is just changing, thanks to AI, thanks to agents and their introduction into the corporate environment. The internet is full of opinions and ideas that push and pull and prod people in different directions. And every one of those ideas has contexts, which is necessary to keep in mind when filtering the ideas. At a smaller startup where you can have a $200 a month Claude Code subscription for all of your engineers, that’s gonna yield certain results that’s going to encourage and invite certain people into that space to use those tools, the clawed tools, or Gemini or Codex. I work at a big company, Caterpillar. We have a GitHub co-pilot, but through co-pilot we have access to the kind of frontier large language models. From there, we have access to the co-pilot harness, whether it’s co-pilot CLI or the co-pilot integration with Visual Studio code, or the other IDEs like JetBrains, et cetera. Out there in the world, he has certain opinions from some people. You have people who are very pro agents like Steve Yeage, who has been a big influence to me over the last several months, as I’ve definitely jumped into the deep end of agentic coding. I haven’t even really opened my IDD in months, except for small things that I want to do by hand. enterprise grade work for the last three months or so and maybe a little longer has been fully written and produced by agents and i’ve been using AI to write code to some capacity or another since chad gpt came out really since like claude sonnet 3.5 but this thinking that i am doing is It’s really supposed to be about me, so this blog post I want to write is me processing thoughts on the expectation change that’s placed on developers in certain environments for certain types of work. I guess even that, like that sounds kind of vague. So I can only speak to myself. So I need to put a big annotation and plaster this blog post with this big caveat message that this is me, this is my experience, this is my position, and this is not a truth that is wide reaching. It’s not any kind of prediction on the, you know, the larger change happening in the world. This is just where I am at. So maybe for the post to make sense, I need to give a brief amount of history about me and my work. I’m not a trained software engineer, but I’ve been, I guess I’ve been a pretty impressive asset in my employment. I’ve been at Caterpillar for nine years, and in that nine years or over in the last several years, I’ve moonlit, moonlighted a little bit. And at every place I’ve done any other amount of work, I’ve just consistently impressed people. Now, this really just leads me to have more imposter syndrome because I know or I have learned what impresses people, And it isn’t necessarily excellence, although I try to do things well and I want to solve problems and maintain the systems that I build to solve those problems. But I don’t write the best code. I’m not the smartest developer. I don’t know the most. I get to know the things I work with and I learn a lot and I work fast because I have Not a super unique, but a rare ability to focus in, when the stars align, to focus and produce more than the next person. Not every next person, but a lot of the next people, a lot of the people I work with, I outperform. And that’s been true, or it has seemed true, from every review, pretty much every review I’ve ever received, that’s been true. And as I’ve had that just personal truth be reflected in my work, it’s been enhanced with AI because I’ve been an early adopter and even as a, even as somewhat of a skeptic, like I’ve tried to maintain a posture of skepticism. But since Opus 4.5, Even though I might talk like a skeptic, I am leaning into agents hard. And I am practicing my own harness engineering with my nexus project. And I’m using it to do engineering work at Caterpillar that’s going into production for us, which is like data platform type of work. It’s not custom, it’s not external customer facing. It’s internal tooling, which is what I mostly built. And the thing I’m really trying to wrap my head around, or I guess I’m trying to explain, is without AI, I was out producing a lot of people. And with AI, you can produce just a shit ton of code. And I’m trying to do that part well, but in my own gifts and curses of hyper focus and Wanting to meet expectations and solve problems, I’m jumping into the new frontier very quickly. But something I’ve noticed is that as I’ve produced a lot, people are just impressed. And they’re not necessarily impressed with the excellence. They’re impressed with how I talk about things. They’re impressed with how much I do, and they’re impressed with the output they see. But the result of a bunch of code isn’t all of the code itself. And I haven’t read all the code I’ve produced with agents. I’ve certainly tried to test most of it or had most of it tested. But as I’ve sought to do this and as I’ve been working in this capacity of using agents very heavily, I just feel kind of torn. in trusting the agents and in working with the agents in the ways that I think are appropriate, but also collaborating with other humans who are also using AI. But are they using AI in a trustworthy way? I don’t know, and I’m not sure how to validate it. But my managers seem to think I know how to validate it, and they seem impressed with the work I do, and they seem impressed with my understanding of AI and agentic coding. And so I feel all of this pressure to continue to be a top performer like I have been since before AI. I feel a lot of pressure to, I don’t want to coach people in how I do things, but I’m being asked to coach people and how I do things because other people I work with notice me. And I guess I’m almost, I’m just kind of tired of being noticed. Because being noticed is not resulting in me becoming rich. And money is not the most important thing. But man, I’d love to just make enough money to fuck off for the rest of my life and never look at a computer ever again. I would love… to not have to continue to maintain systems that I build or that other people build or to collaborate with people I don’t know, who might not even be long term. That’s the one thing about Caterpillar is I’m working with a lot of contractors. And nothing wrong with contracting, I’ve done that. Nothing wrong with being a contractor, but They could disappear at any moment, and all the code that they write, and even today, all the code that they prompt and have an agent right becomes my problem, my maintenance issue, my responsibility. And it just is, It’s just making me nervous to maintain and to understand and to continue to work under conditions that I can’t even tell if I’m making them for myself or if they’re real expectations. Like if I fell off the face of the earth or if I dropped agentic coding entirely and I just went back to coding by hand completely, would my output continue to impress people today? I don’t know the answer to that. But I certainly wouldn’t be solving problems as fast, but would I be creating less problems? Like I’ve solved a lot of problems in three months in my new role here with Forge. But I don’t know how many problems I’ve created. Only time will tell. And the thing is, the guys I work with who are contractors, they might not be around long enough for time to tell, but because I’m not rich yet, I probably will be long enough, or be around long enough. to experience those bugs and those problems that I don’t know about yet. And I am just feeling so much pressure to be the best and to be the one to solve problems. And I don’t know if I’m putting it on me or if cat’s putting it on me or if my project manager is putting it on me. I’m just really struggling with the amount of responsibility I feel. And I’m feeling frustrated about it because that amount of responsibility feels like it has scaled a lot with agents, with AI, but not my paycheck. And in fact, my paycheck has gone down quite a bit. And I’m not more relaxed. I’m making about half of what I’ve made over the last couple of years. And I’m not more relaxed. I don’t feel freer. I don’t feel like I have 50% of the responsibility that I did. Cal Autonomy awoke something in me for purpose, but that feels like it’s already starting to die. I’m already tired. I’m, I don’t know about burnt out, but I’m tired. I was reviewing some code that one of these contractors I’m working with. It’s actually only an intern. He’s not even a contractor. He’s an intern. And I’m reviewing a pull request of his. And damn, it’s a lot of code. And it looks somewhat useful. But I don’t know exactly how to test it. That’s not true actually, I do know how to test it, but I don’t own enough of our infrastructure at Caterpillar to test it easily. So do I trust him? Do I trust his prompt? Do I trust his harness? Do I trust the tests that I have already put in the code base to capture and block any breakages he might have introduced with this code for the code I’ve already been producing? It’s different when I’m intimately familiar with the code base. And I’ve been, I don’t know, definitely two other places at least where I had very intimate familiarity with the system and with the code and with the platform. But the one I’m on right now is new, and I built it. I built it with agents. I built it to replace a thing that was never even working. But I built it. It’s mine. It’s not somebody else’s. It’s not that we’ll document it. There’s a lot of documentation, but it’s all been agent produced, and even though I’ve reviewed it, it’s hard for me to organize it in the right way in a way that makes sense. I’m just feeling so frustrated that it seems like, as the tools are getting better, as developers are able to move faster, it feels like I am expected to move faster. but I’m not expected to make any more money. I’m not expected to be compensated anymore for the increase in velocity and responsibility. It’s almost like if I could produce, this metric is not gonna be real, but let’s just, for the sake of argument, make it up. If I can write 30,000 lines of code in a year and make $100,000, I feel fine about that, whatever that number means. But now I can actually produce 300,000 lines of code in a year. I’m definitely producing 10 times more code than normal. I don’t know if I’m doing 10 times more engineering, but I am making exactly the same amount of money. And so why did I do it? Why am I leaning into it so hard? Why am I trying to still be the front runner to be on the bleeding edge when caterpillar is not going to pay anymore? And I could go somewhere else. I could go to Avant. I could make more. It’s a system I’m familiar with. It’s even people I know. And there’s AI there too. But it’s a system I know. It’s a system I know how to support and maintain. And there’s not an expectation that I’m going to produce 10,000 lines of code this week. But right now at Caterpillar, it feels like I am expected to write 10,000 lines of code this week. And deploy it and maintain it and solve new problems. All in an incredibly political and hectic, chaotic environment where there isn’t an appropriate amount of leadership over me. I am the expert in AI in my group. And that feels retarded. I am the professional agentic engineer and that is just scary because I’m not good enough to be that. I’m not Steve Yeagie, I’m not Simon Willison, I haven’t been a developer for 20 years. I’m just a guy who learned some Python to solve some problems and happen to work faster than a lot of people and that reputation has really It’s treated me well for sure. And my disposition to problem solving has, up until recently, I felt like I had been, like I’ve been compensated well by my company, but then I’ve also been able to do more work outside of one job for me to feel the value of my own skills. But now with AI changing everything, Can I show you what’s on the back of my story? It feels like I’ve given up the personal gains. One second, Alia. So I’ve given up personally realizing the benefit of my own skill. And now I am like in a position where Caterpillar, and only Caterpillar, is reaping the benefit of my new scheme in agentic engineering. And I think that’s just ticking me off because I stayed with Catt to do something good for the world. And I think we can do something good for the world. But I’m tired.

Notes and Summarization #

Possible Titles #

  • Agents, Responsibility, and the Cost of Going Faster
  • The Irony of 10x
  • More Output, Less Upside
  • When AI Made Me Faster and Poorer
  • Being Crushed by Responsibility

Working Angle #

This should probably be a personal essay, not a manifesto about AI. The core tension:

  • agents made me dramatically more productive
  • that productivity increased the responsibility I carry
  • the financial upside I used to realize personally has gone down, not up

Section Stub: Opening Scene #

Prompt:

  • Start with a concrete moment. Maybe reviewing a massive PR from the intern / contractor side of the system.
  • What did I feel in that moment: confusion, dread, pressure, responsibility, skepticism?
  • What was the specific thought: “I might own all of this later, even if I did not really produce or validate all of it myself.”
  • Can I open with one sharp sentence that names the tension right away?

Possible opener idea:

“Agentic coding has made me faster than ever, but it has also made me feel responsible for more than I can honestly hold in my head.”

Section Stub: This Is About Me, Not Everyone #

Prompt:

  • Add a strong caveat early: this is not prediction, prescription, or universal truth.
  • Name my context: big company, internal platform work, political environment, mixed team ownership, frontier models via Copilot.
  • What about my temperament matters here? Hyperfocus, initiative, problem solving, pressure sensitivity, desire to meet expectations.
  • What would I want a reader to not mishear?

Section Stub: Who I Was Before Agents #

Prompt:

  • Briefly describe my work history and self-understanding.
  • I am not formally trained, so what made me valuable anyway?
  • What does it mean that people were impressed before AI too?
  • Pull in relevant threads from pages/blog/forge-ahead.md: prior projects, practical problem solving, being useful, learning systems by doing.
  • What gifts do I think God gave me that made me effective before this shift?

Questions to answer:

  • What kind of worker was I before agents entered my workflow?
  • What did I already know how to do well?
  • What part of my value came from focus rather than brilliance?

Section Stub: Why I Leaned Into Agentic Coding #

Prompt:

  • Explain that I did not stumble into this accidentally; I chose to go hard.
  • Why did it feel natural to me to adopt agents aggressively?
  • What about the mission at Caterpillar Autonomy made the leap feel worth it?
  • Pull in pages/blog/cat-autonomy-2-0.md: I stayed because the work felt meaningful, not merely because it was interesting.
  • Mention harness engineering / Nexus / experimentation if it helps show this was a deliberate investment.

Questions to answer:

  • Why did I trust this direction enough to reorganize my work around it?
  • Was I chasing novelty, usefulness, recognition, mission, or all of the above?

Section Stub: What Actually Changed #

Prompt:

  • Describe the practical change in my day-to-day work.
  • I am no longer mainly writing code line by line; I am directing, reviewing, testing, and integrating generated work.
  • What changed about the quantity of output?
  • What changed about how coworkers and managers perceived me?
  • What changed about the kind of questions people started asking me?

Questions to answer:

  • When did I realize this was not just autocomplete, but a new mode of working?
  • What does “enterprise-grade work fully written and produced by agents” actually mean in practice?

Section Stub: The Hidden Cost of Speed #

Prompt:

  • Write about the gap between output and understanding.
  • I can ship more, but I do not always know the code as intimately as hand-written systems I built before.
  • Testing is not the same as ownership.
  • Documentation existing is not the same as confidence.
  • What kinds of future problems does speed create?

Questions to answer:

  • What do I know I have not fully read?
  • What kinds of bugs or maintenance traps am I afraid I am creating?
  • What does it feel like to build something that works but still feels partially foreign?

Section Stub: Responsibility Without Clear Boundaries #

Prompt:

  • This may be the emotional center before the money section.
  • Describe the contractor / intern dynamic and why it intensifies the burden.
  • Their output can become my long-term maintenance problem.
  • The organization sees me as someone who understands AI and agents, so responsibility pools onto me.
  • Ask whether the pressure is explicit or self-imposed, but note that the body feels it either way.

Questions to answer:

  • Who is actually accountable when AI-assisted code breaks six months from now?
  • What does it mean to be treated like the local expert when I do not feel like one?
  • Why is being noticed beginning to feel costly instead of rewarding?

Section Stub: The Financial Irony #

Prompt:

  • State this clearly and concretely.
  • For years, I realized more value from my output because I worked two jobs concurrently.
  • Due to the new role, new responsibility, and the demands of agentic coding in this environment, I had to go down to one job.
  • So the irony is: the tools make me dramatically more productive, but I personally realize less economic upside from my own gifts and skills than I did before.
  • Keep this grounded and honest, not whiny.

Questions to answer:

  • What exactly have I lost financially?
  • Why does this feel bigger than “I want more money”?
  • Where do the gains of AI go when an individual contributor gets faster?
  • If I can now produce 10x more code, why does my life not feel lighter, freer, or better compensated?

Possible thesis sentence:

“Agentic coding increased the value I create at work, while decreasing the share of that value I personally get to realize.”

Section Stub: Mission, Meaning, and Fatigue #

Prompt:

  • Reaffirm the good: this is meaningful work, and that matters to me.
  • Tie back to autonomy, safety, and the reasons I stayed at Caterpillar.
  • Then tell the truth: meaning does not cancel fatigue.
  • What has already started to feel tired, dulled, or overdrawn in me?

Questions to answer:

  • What purpose did this role awaken in me?
  • Why does that sense of purpose already feel threatened?
  • How do I talk honestly about fatigue without pretending I am fully burned out if I am not sure?

Section Stub: Questions I Cannot Yet Answer #

Prompt:

  • Let the essay breathe here instead of forcing a neat conclusion.
  • Gather the real unresolved questions.
  • If I stopped using agents, would I still impress people?
  • Would I solve fewer problems or create fewer future ones?
  • Am I carrying real expectations or anticipated ones?
  • Is this making me a better engineer, or just a faster source of output and responsibility?

Section Stub: Conclusion #

Prompt:

  • End modestly, not with a manifesto.
  • I am not anti-AI.
  • I am not saying agents are bad.
  • I am trying to tell the truth about what this transition has cost me personally.
  • Land on the mismatch between speed, responsibility, and reward.

Possible closing direction:

  • The tools are real.
  • The gains are real.
  • The responsibility is real.
  • The redistribution of value is also real.
  • I am still trying to understand what faithfulness looks like inside that tension.

Material To Weave In #

  • My lack of formal software engineering background
  • My history of being useful by solving practical problems quickly
  • My tendency toward hyperfocus and over-responsibility
  • The shift from hand-written confidence to agent-mediated uncertainty
  • The contractor / intern maintenance concern
  • The drop from two incomes to one
  • The irony that Cat benefits more from my increased output than I do
  • The Christian framing around calling, providence, stewardship, and fatigue

Things To Avoid #

  • sounding like I am making universal claims about all AI use
  • sounding bitter without being specific
  • centering line-count metrics too much without translating them into responsibility
  • pretending I have fully landed on a conclusion
  • making this a complaint post about coworkers instead of a reflection on burden and change

And so I feel all of this pressure to continue to be a top performer like I have been since before AI.
I feel a lot of pressure to, I don't want to coach people in how I do things, but I'm being asked to coach people and how I do things because other people I work with notice me.
And I guess I'm almost, I'm just kind of tired of being noticed.
Because being noticed is not resulting in me becoming rich.
And money is not the most important thing.
But man, I'd love to just make enough money to fuck off for the rest of my life and never look at a computer ever again.
I would love...
to not have to continue to maintain systems that I build or that other people build or to collaborate with people I don't know, who might not even be long term.
That's the one thing about Caterpillar is I'm working with a lot of contractors.
And nothing wrong with contracting, I've done that.
Nothing wrong with being a contractor, but
They could disappear at any moment, and all the code that they write, and even today, all the code that they prompt and have an agent right becomes my problem, my maintenance issue, my responsibility.
And it just is,
It's just making me nervous to maintain and to understand and to continue to work under conditions that I can't even tell if I'm making them for myself or if they're real expectations.
Like if I fell off the face of the earth or if I dropped agentic coding entirely and I just went back to coding by hand completely, would my output continue to impress people today?
I don't know the answer to that.
But I certainly wouldn't be solving problems as fast, but would I be creating less problems?
Like I've solved a lot of problems in three months in my new role here with Forge.
But I don't know how many problems I've created.
Only time will tell.
And the thing is, the guys I work with who are contractors, they might not be around long enough for time to tell, but because I'm not rich yet, I probably will be long enough, or be around long enough.
to experience those bugs and those problems that I don't know about yet.
And I am just feeling so much pressure to be the best and to be the one to solve problems.
And I don't know if I'm putting it on me or if cat's putting it on me or if my project manager is putting it on me.
I'm just really struggling with the amount of responsibility I feel.
And I'm feeling frustrated about it because that amount of responsibility feels like it has scaled a lot with agents, with AI, but not my paycheck.
And in fact, my paycheck has gone down quite a bit.
And I'm not more relaxed.
I'm making about half of what I've made over the last couple of years.
And I'm not more relaxed.
I don't feel freer.
I don't feel like I have 50% of the responsibility that I did.
Cal Autonomy awoke something in me for purpose, but that feels like it's already starting to die.
I'm already tired.
I'm, I don't know about burnt out, but I'm tired.
I was reviewing some code that one of these contractors I'm working with.
It's actually only an intern.
He's not even a contractor.
He's an intern.
And I'm reviewing a pull request of his.
And damn, it's a lot of code.
And it looks somewhat useful.
But I don't know exactly how to test it.
That's not true actually, I do know how to test it, but I don't own enough of our infrastructure at Caterpillar to test it easily.
So do I trust him?
Do I trust his prompt?
Do I trust his harness?
Do I trust the tests that I have already put in the code base to capture and block any breakages he might have introduced with this code for the code I've already been producing?
It's different when I'm intimately familiar with the code base.
And I've been, I don't know, definitely two other places at least where I had very intimate familiarity with the system and with the code and with the platform.
But the one I'm on right now is new, and I built it.
I built it with agents.
I built it to replace a thing that was never even working.
But I built it.
It's mine.
It's not somebody else's.
It's not that we'll document it.
There's a lot of documentation, but it's all been agent produced, and even though I've reviewed it, it's hard for me to organize it in the right way in a way that makes sense.
I'm just feeling so frustrated that it seems like, as the tools are getting better, as developers are able to move faster, it feels like I am expected to move faster.
but I'm not expected to make any more money.
I'm not expected to be compensated anymore for the increase in velocity and responsibility.
It's almost like if I could produce, this metric is not gonna be real, but let's just, for the sake of argument, make it up.
If I can write 30,000 lines of code in a year and make $100,000, I feel fine about that, whatever that number means.
But now I can actually produce 300,000 lines of code in a year.
I'm definitely producing 10 times more code than normal.
I don't know if I'm doing 10 times more engineering, but I am making exactly the same amount of money.
And so why did I do it?
Why am I leaning into it so hard?
Why am I trying to still be the front runner to be on the bleeding edge when caterpillar is not going to pay anymore?
And I could go somewhere else.
I could go to Avant.
I could make more.
It's a system I'm familiar with.
It's even people I know.
And there's AI there too.
But it's a system I know.
It's a system I know how to support and maintain.
And there's not an expectation that I'm going to produce 10,000 lines of code this week.
But right now at Caterpillar, it feels like I am expected to write 10,000 lines of code this week.
And deploy it and maintain it and solve new problems.
All in an incredibly political and hectic, chaotic environment where there isn't an appropriate amount of leadership over me.
I am the expert in AI in my group.
And that feels retarded.
I am the professional agentic engineer and that is just scary because I'm not good enough to be that.
I'm not Steve Yeagie, I'm not Simon Willison, I haven't been a developer for 20 years.
I'm just a guy who learned some Python to solve some problems and happen to work faster than a lot of people and that reputation has really
It's treated me well for sure.
And my disposition to problem solving has, up until recently, I felt like I had been, like I've been compensated well by my company, but then I've also been able to do more work outside of one job for me to feel the value of my own skills.
But now with AI changing everything,
Can I show you what's on the back of my story?
It feels like I've given up the personal gains.
One second, Alia.
So I've given up personally realizing the benefit of my own skill.
And now I am like in a position where
Caterpillar, and only Caterpillar, is reaping the benefit of my new scheme in agentic engineering.
And I think that's just ticking me off because I stayed with Catt to do something good for the world.
And I think we can do something good for the world.
But I'm tired.

## Notes and Summarization

## Possible Titles

- Agents, Responsibility, and the Cost of Going Faster
- The Irony of 10x
- More Output, Less Upside
- When AI Made Me Faster and Poorer
- Being Crushed by Responsibility

## Working Angle

This should probably be a personal essay, not a manifesto about AI. The core tension:

- agents made me dramatically more productive
- that productivity increased the responsibility I carry
- the financial upside I used to realize personally has gone down, not up

## Section Stub: Opening Scene

Prompt:

- Start with a concrete moment. Maybe reviewing a massive PR from the intern / contractor side of the system.
- What did I feel in that moment: confusion, dread, pressure, responsibility, skepticism?
- What was the specific thought: "I might own all of this later, even if I did not really produce or validate all of it myself."
- Can I open with one sharp sentence that names the tension right away?

Possible opener idea:

"Agentic coding has made me faster than ever, but it has also made me feel responsible for more than I can honestly hold in my head."

## Section Stub: This Is About Me, Not Everyone

Prompt:

- Add a strong caveat early: this is not prediction, prescription, or universal truth.
- Name my context: big company, internal platform work, political environment, mixed team ownership, frontier models via Copilot.
- What about my temperament matters here? Hyperfocus, initiative, problem solving, pressure sensitivity, desire to meet expectations.
- What would I want a reader to not mishear?

## Section Stub: Who I Was Before Agents

Prompt:

- Briefly describe my work history and self-understanding.
- I am not formally trained, so what made me valuable anyway?
- What does it mean that people were impressed before AI too?
- Pull in relevant threads from `pages/blog/forge-ahead.md`: prior projects, practical problem solving, being useful, learning systems by doing.
- What gifts do I think God gave me that made me effective before this shift?

Questions to answer:

- What kind of worker was I before agents entered my workflow?
- What did I already know how to do well?
- What part of my value came from focus rather than brilliance?

## Section Stub: Why I Leaned Into Agentic Coding

Prompt:

- Explain that I did not stumble into this accidentally; I chose to go hard.
- Why did it feel natural to me to adopt agents aggressively?
- What about the mission at Caterpillar Autonomy made the leap feel worth it?
- Pull in `pages/blog/cat-autonomy-2-0.md`: I stayed because the work felt meaningful, not merely because it was interesting.
- Mention harness engineering / Nexus / experimentation if it helps show this was a deliberate investment.

Questions to answer:

- Why did I trust this direction enough to reorganize my work around it?
- Was I chasing novelty, usefulness, recognition, mission, or all of the above?

## Section Stub: What Actually Changed

Prompt:

- Describe the practical change in my day-to-day work.
- I am no longer mainly writing code line by line; I am directing, reviewing, testing, and integrating generated work.
- What changed about the quantity of output?
- What changed about how coworkers and managers perceived me?
- What changed about the kind of questions people started asking me?

Questions to answer:

- When did I realize this was not just autocomplete, but a new mode of working?
- What does "enterprise-grade work fully written and produced by agents" actually mean in practice?

## Section Stub: The Hidden Cost of Speed

Prompt:

- Write about the gap between output and understanding.
- I can ship more, but I do not always know the code as intimately as hand-written systems I built before.
- Testing is not the same as ownership.
- Documentation existing is not the same as confidence.
- What kinds of future problems does speed create?

Questions to answer:

- What do I know I have not fully read?
- What kinds of bugs or maintenance traps am I afraid I am creating?
- What does it feel like to build something that works but still feels partially foreign?

## Section Stub: Responsibility Without Clear Boundaries

Prompt:

- This may be the emotional center before the money section.
- Describe the contractor / intern dynamic and why it intensifies the burden.
- Their output can become my long-term maintenance problem.
- The organization sees me as someone who understands AI and agents, so responsibility pools onto me.
- Ask whether the pressure is explicit or self-imposed, but note that the body feels it either way.

Questions to answer:

- Who is actually accountable when AI-assisted code breaks six months from now?
- What does it mean to be treated like the local expert when I do not feel like one?
- Why is being noticed beginning to feel costly instead of rewarding?

## Section Stub: The Financial Irony

Prompt:

- State this clearly and concretely.
- For years, I realized more value from my output because I worked two jobs concurrently.
- Due to the new role, new responsibility, and the demands of agentic coding in this environment, I had to go down to one job.
- So the irony is: the tools make me dramatically more productive, but I personally realize less economic upside from my own gifts and skills than I did before.
- Keep this grounded and honest, not whiny.

Questions to answer:

- What exactly have I lost financially?
- Why does this feel bigger than "I want more money"?
- Where do the gains of AI go when an individual contributor gets faster?
- If I can now produce 10x more code, why does my life not feel lighter, freer, or better compensated?

Possible thesis sentence:

"Agentic coding increased the value I create at work, while decreasing the share of that value I personally get to realize."

## Section Stub: Mission, Meaning, and Fatigue

Prompt:

- Reaffirm the good: this is meaningful work, and that matters to me.
- Tie back to autonomy, safety, and the reasons I stayed at Caterpillar.
- Then tell the truth: meaning does not cancel fatigue.
- What has already started to feel tired, dulled, or overdrawn in me?

Questions to answer:

- What purpose did this role awaken in me?
- Why does that sense of purpose already feel threatened?
- How do I talk honestly about fatigue without pretending I am fully burned out if I am not sure?

## Section Stub: Questions I Cannot Yet Answer

Prompt:

- Let the essay breathe here instead of forcing a neat conclusion.
- Gather the real unresolved questions.
- If I stopped using agents, would I still impress people?
- Would I solve fewer problems or create fewer future ones?
- Am I carrying real expectations or anticipated ones?
- Is this making me a better engineer, or just a faster source of output and responsibility?

## Section Stub: Conclusion

Prompt:

- End modestly, not with a manifesto.
- I am not anti-AI.
- I am not saying agents are bad.
- I am trying to tell the truth about what this transition has cost me personally.
- Land on the mismatch between speed, responsibility, and reward.

Possible closing direction:

- The tools are real.
- The gains are real.
- The responsibility is real.
- The redistribution of value is also real.
- I am still trying to understand what faithfulness looks like inside that tension.

## Material To Weave In

- My lack of formal software engineering background
- My history of being useful by solving practical problems quickly
- My tendency toward hyperfocus and over-responsibility
- The shift from hand-written confidence to agent-mediated uncertainty
- The contractor / intern maintenance concern
- The drop from two incomes to one
- The irony that Cat benefits more from my increased output than I do
- The Christian framing around calling, providence, stewardship, and fatigue

## Things To Avoid

- sounding like I am making universal claims about all AI use
- sounding bitter without being specific
- centering line-count metrics too much without translating them into responsibility
- pretending I have fully landed on a conclusion
- making this a complaint post about coworkers instead of a reflection on burden and change

items.title: I Was Saved From A Cult
items.content_html:
Introduction #

I’m getting coffee with a guy from church today, we’re planning to swap some stories about how the Lord has worked in our lives in a few specific ways. He has some history in the New Age movement, and I’m very interested in that story. My offering to him will be my own story, fairly short it might be, of how God protected me from long-term involvement in a hypercharasmatic cult.

Theological Context #

This dove-tails well with Andrew’s sermon yesterday, noting that in many Charasmatic circles the gift of the Holy Spirit becomes more important than the person of Jesus who gives the Spirit, and who gives Salvation. This is the crux of my own experience as well.

The Group #

The group was called “Wind and Fire Ministries” and they had their own purpose-built building out in the middle of nowhere, but close enough for me to drive to. I grew up in Iowa, a 10 minute drive on the interstate landed you pretty quick in the scene of any low-budget horror movie. The building was definitely nice, there was even some land, but there was nothing around it.

How I Got Involved #

I barely remember how I got involved - a kid I was in high school with went there regularly and then one adult who helped out in my church’s youth group did as well. I can still vividly remember him telling me about an experience he had at this place - a “slayed in the spirit” kind of experience.

My Experience #

I was hungry, desperate even, for spiritual experiences and this “ministry” was extremely welcoming and accessible. My parents didn’t know anything about what went on there, and to be fair they didn’t do a ton of ultra-weird stuff when I was there… flag-waving and tongues were enough to probably ruffle some fundie feathers. I never fell to the ground shaking or spoke in tongues (not for lack of awkwardly trying upon the instruction of a member there though). I remember going one night and staying for hours while the head honcho was doing annointings with oil and I wanted to be annointed because I wanted to speak in tongues because I wanted an “experience”. By God’s grace I was never given a super emotional experience there - the emphasis was always on gifts and supernatural things, not on the person and work of the Lord Jesus

items.title: I’m back from the dead
items.content_html:
The flu hit me like a freight train right at the start of the year, along with the most stress I’ve ever felt at work dropping on me at the same time, I’ve been out of commission for what feels like forever. But this week I’ve been bouncing back and I feel like a million bucks now… and a lot has happened

This post isn’t a review, it’s a note for me to come back and build on with some more posts probably. My life has been a bit chaotic but in God’s good grace on my life, that chaos hasn’t ruined anything (I am still wrestling with one aspect of it) but something’s changed this year… I’m not only back from the flu over the last several weeks, I feel like I’ve been resurrected as a developer. I’d written a few times last summer, feeling like I was in a rut, and I felt good coming out of that low season, but as I’ve reflected it’s really the last couple of years have been a slow descent into, not into depression, but something akin to it…

Not only is that season either over or on pause, cause I’ve been buzzin on building things for a week now like I can hardly remember, but I’ve had some significant work changes. Longer reflection post to come - but after much toil I am actually back in Caterpillar Autonomy, a group I left from burn-out 5 years ago. In fact, I’m on the same project, but with new eyes, new passion, new knowledge and experience, and the fun part for me now is new tools. AI hasn’t been my friend the whole time, I’ve vibe-coded some disasters, pseudo-vibe-coded some cool stuff, but ultimately it’s not been a net positive for me until this week. Getting a workflow ironed out in order to keep up with the group’s pace, or the pace I want us to be at, has been exciting and I swear I’ve done a month’s work of work since Monday… no hype, no selling, just letting you know that AI can’t do it all, but with good design it sure can generate some code that doesn’t suck.

So… I’m back, almost from the dead, and it’s January 23 but let’s kick 2026 right in the cajones!

items.title: Homelabbing Realization - Configs and Git
items.content_html:
Realization #

I’m back to brainstorming migrations away from Docker Compose to something that solves multi-node networking and secrets but I don’t want to go to k8s… so my options are probably Docker Swarm or Nomad. As I wrestle mentally here I was thinking about one of my issues with multi-node setup is that I still keep everything out of one git repo, so if something gets managed remotely then I get out of sync. Best example is dashy, Due to some constraint of wanting to be as close to zero-day deployment-ready as possible, I think I overcomplicate some of the simple stuff - like it’s ok to just have to put a file on a server for a container to start the first time… That doesn’t mean ansible is a requirement, in fact lately I’ve just leaned into just recipes. But even then, I cornered myself into tracking my dashy config in git, so I’m hesitant to ever update it in the browser cause I’ll have to redownload the config, reconcile the formatting differences in my repo (there’s a reason for this that a linter doesn’t ssolve…), etc…. but in all of my brainstorming I just decided that my dashy config doesn’t have to live in git… it can just be on the zfs storage, which is backed up, and configured via the app itself… the config can simply be apart of the data and container lifecycle, it doesn’t have to be apart of the infra lifecycle.

items.title: Facism and Heresy - Words Matter
items.content_html:
This is a short reflection/semi-open letter to a friend I’ve been having a conversation with for a couple weeks

Name-calling in a rhetorical exchange is such a school-yard bully, low IQ, desperate, degenerate move when it’s used in lieu of data… I have 2 scenarios in my head that bring light to one another.

Warning

Today the words “Nazi” and “Facist” are so over-used it’s moved beyond sickening to boring.

However, the usage of these words has led to violence, and a lot of it in my opinion. The dangerous rhetoric is a key player in the multiple Trump-assassination attempts, various acts of violence against other conservatives, specifically, (because who else does the Left call a Facist except anyone remotely moderate anymore), and most notably the murder of Charlie Kirk. I find the rhetoric super dangerous because I’m not a politician, but boy can I tell you for sure that Charlie was a moderate, and if they came for him then consider my reflection: Reflection - They Can Come For Anyone.

One of the problems I see here is that many people can’t define “Nazi” or “Facist”. To the Left, these words just describe someone they disagree with, and it’s turning out - ultimately someone they think would be better off dead.

It reminds me of a kid at a summer camp I worked at about 10 years ago. The camp was all about Christian apologetics - great times, good discussions, lots of great content, etc. One year there was a 17 or 18 year old boy here, super fundamentalist in his beliefs… no harm no foul here. But he demonstrated a habit of calling anything that differ’ed from his interpretation of a passage of scripture as heresy. Now… here’s the thing, it’s not heresy to not be a young-earth-creationist. But something that is true is that people have been put to death over heresy in the history of the Church…. and yet this kid felt comfortable labeling anyone a heretic who was more fluent in Hebrew than him…

So what do I see? - There’s similarities between that immature kid and practically anyone using the words “Nazi” or “Facist” to describe American politics right now - are the same type of person to me. That person feels a deep care for the thing they think they’re protecting, but in reality they’re participating in a violent pattern of history that they do not understand

So to us today, in or out of the Church, involved or not involved with politics… We need to recognize that words matter. And to carelessly use words that eventually excuse violence is at best, ignorant. There’s nothing wrong with ignorance, but a good measure of a man is what he does when his ignorance has been pointed out… Will you be apart of the solution? Or continue to fan the flames?

items.title: Questions for Dad about the Navy
items.content_html:
Submarine Life #

  1. What did a typical day look like when the submarine was underway?
  2. How did the 18-hour day with 6-hour shifts affect everyone’s sense of time?
  3. How did you and the crew keep busy or entertained during long patrols?
  4. Can you describe the living quarters? What was the hardest part about the limited space?
  5. What meals do you remember best?

The Job #

  1. What systems were you directly responsible for as a machinist?
  2. How did your team monitor and maintain the reactor? Any emergency drills that stick out?
  3. What’s the most challenging mechanical problem you dealt with on the sub?
  4. What kind of training did you receive before serving underwater? How did reality differ?
  5. What did it take to “earn your dolphins”?

Technology #

  1. What pieces of technology or engineering challenges stand out from working with the reactor?
  2. How were water, air, and electricity produced and maintained?
  3. Did you work with any systems that have since been declassified?
  4. What mechanical or safety upgrades have been made since your time that you wish you’d had?

The Experience #

  1. What kind of camaraderie did you develop with the crew?
  2. Did your team face any emergencies or close calls with the reactor?
  3. How did you cope with being underwater for long periods?
  4. Were there any traditions or unwritten rules among the machinists?
  5. What was the relationship like between machinists, electricians, and other crew?
  6. If you could go back, what advice would you give to someone starting as a machinist on a nuclear sub today?

1 John 3: 7-10 for men’s group in August 2025

1 John 3: 7-10

7 Little children, let no one deceive you: the one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as that one is righteous. 8 The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. For this reason the Son of God was revealed: in order to destroy the works of the devil. 9 Everyone who is fathered by God does not practice sin, because his seed resides in him, and he is not able to sin, because he has been fathered by God. 10 By this the children of God and the children of the devil are evident: everyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, namely, the one who does not love his brother.

verse 7 from ESV

7 Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous

The difference I note is that ESV, right or wrong, is more clear that the “just as that one is righteous” is actually Jesus

Flowchart #

affine link

Interesting notes #

  • we will avoid cheap questions that assume black and white understanding of the passage “the one who practices sin if of the devil” does not mean that sinning one time means you’re not saved… put the juvenile things behind us
  • “the devil has been sinning from the beginning”
    • from the beginning of what?
    • has he really been sinning the entire time? don’t we have mythology about Lucifer being an angel of light??? (note the heavy sarcasm from me here…)

Reflection #

I’ve been loosely mediating on this and Romans 7 and 8

Romans 7:16-8:11

15 For what I am doing I do not understand, because what I want to do, this I do not practice, but what I hate, this I do. 16 Now if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good. 17 So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. 18 For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh. For I have the desire to do what is right, but not the ability to carry it out. 19 For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing. 20 Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. 21 So I find it to be a law that when I want to do right, evil lies close at hand. 22 For I delight in the law of God, in my inner being, 23 but I see in my members another law waging war against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that dwells in my members. 24 Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death? 25 Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin. 8:1 There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. 2 For the law of the Spirit of life has set you free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death. 3 For God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do. By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh, 4 in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. 5 For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit. 6 For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace. 7 For the mind that is set on the flesh is hostile to God, for it does not submit to God’s law; indeed, it cannot. 8 Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. 9 You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. 10 But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. 11 If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.

I think I’m mostly walking away from these texts with 2 things on my heart:

  1. I must be desensitized to some sin in my life - I think it’s impossible for me to know in my inner being am I genuinely separating myself from my sinfulness and enjoying God’s presence, or am I using grace as an excuse to sin… The entanglement of my own heart is one of the most difficult things to navigate in personal faith.
  2. I am questioning my devotion… am I devoted to Jesus, to his law, to doing good… or am I a slave to myself?

As I write this out, the Christian concept of “setting the captives free” and jubilee and freedom strike my heart deeply. Just these phrases begin to call up emotions. But as I look at my life right now, what am I doing that shouts freedom? I spend more time lately playing games than being entrenched in theological study, I think about work more than things which are noble and praiseworthy, and I seem to purposefully focus on my own situations internally rather than on God’s grace (which I do externally a lot - but I feel this tension inside - a hook of doubt)

Romans 8:5a

5 For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh,

Romans 6

6 For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.

Why would I be hesitant to regularly set my mind on things of the spirit? I absolutely feel something inside that rebels against the things of God at times… at odd times as well.

A Prayer #

Lord Jesus, help me to set my mind on things of the Spirit - to live in accordance with your will and righteousness. I confess I run in ways I think are secret or hidden, I reject godly things daily, and yet in your compassionate love you have saved me from this body of sin and death. Praise be to God, guide my heart and mind today, just enough so that tomorrow I can ask for what I need for the day

Romans 8:21-25

21 Consequently, I find the principle with me, the one who wants to do good, that evil is present with me. 22 For I joyfully agree with the law of God in my inner person, 23 but I observe another law in my members, at war with the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that exists in my members. 24 Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death? 25 Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself with my mind am enslaved to the law of God, but with my flesh I am enslaved to the law of sin.

I think I'm mostly walking away from these texts with 2 things on my heart:

1. I must be desensitized to some sin in my life - I think it's impossible for
   me to know in my inner being am I genuinely separating myself from my
sinfulness and enjoying God's presence, or am I using grace as an excuse to
sin... The entanglement of my own heart is one of the most difficult things to
navigate in personal faith.
2. I am questioning my devotion... am I devoted to Jesus, to his law, to doing
   good... or am I a slave to myself?

As I write this out, the Christian concept of "setting the captives free" and
jubilee and freedom strike my heart deeply. Just these phrases begin to call up
emotions. But as I look at my life right now, what am I doing that shouts
freedom? I spend more time lately playing games than being entrenched in
theological study, I think about work more than things which are noble and
praiseworthy, and I seem to purposefully focus on my own situations internally
rather than on God's grace (which I do externally a lot - but I feel this
tension inside - __a hook of doubt__)

??? danger "Romans 8:5a"

    5 For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, 

??? note "Romans 6"

    6 For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.

Why would I be hesitant to regularly set my mind on things of the spirit? I
absolutely feel something inside that rebels against the things of God at
times... at odd times as well.

## A Prayer

Lord Jesus, help me to set my mind on things of the Spirit - to live in
accordance with your will and righteousness. I confess I run in ways I think
are secret or hidden, I reject godly things daily, and yet in your
compassionate love you have saved me from this body of sin and death. Praise be
to God, guide my heart and mind today, just enough so that tomorrow I can ask
for what I need for the day

!!! note "Romans 8:21-25"

    21 Consequently, I find the principle with me, the one who wants to do good, that evil is present with me. 22 For I joyfully agree with the law of God in my inner person, 23 but I observe another law in my members, at war with the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that exists in my members. 24 Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death? 25 Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself with my mind am enslaved to the law of God, but with my flesh I am enslaved to the law of sin.

items.title: Daily Notes Neovim Plugin
items.content_html:
What?

Windsurf helped me whip up a neovim plugin for my daily notes workflows. It has a few features that make my note taking workflow day-to-day a tiny bit more fluid

credit due

Honestly my zettlekasten and this daily notes stuff is only possible with the help of Waylon Walker

Context #

I learned about the concept of a zettlekasten recently and it really spoke to me. I’ve sought for YEARS to have a nice note-taking workflow, where I never think about where to put something, it’s searchable, portable to some degree, and customizable… I’ve used OneNote and its derivatives, different self-hosted container based note taking apps, raw markdown files scattered on my file system, etc… I think I’ve finally landed on a solution which is basically this blog + some tooling to achieve the things I want…

  • markata is the build system, it’s what lets me keep all my notes in markdown files, and build them into a cohesive searchable experience on the web
  • neovim is my primary note taking environment - using tools like marksman I get the ability to “jump” to wiki-linked posts and grep content easily for searching
  • copier is used for generating note templates - whether it’s a til, blog post, or starting my daily note page - copier makes it quick to stub out the file in the right place with the right tags and frontmatter for markata

Usage #

I’ll explain the daily notes workflow here, the code is below…

There’s basically just a couple things I wanted smoothed out in my note-taking as I am getting started here…

  1. I need an immediate way to get to my daily notes page… I have started keeping a new note for each day and it’s a chore to copy paste the old note, update the date, delete content, etc… instead check_and_open_daily_note checks the directory I keep my daily notes in pages/daily in my blog repo, checks the date for a note for today and either creates it from the copier template or opened it as my current buffer

I could maybe improve this by making it global so that no matter what directory I’m in I could open the daily note with a keymap or lua function call instead of swapping tmux sessions and then opening the file

  1. I need a way to link to yesterday’s notes so it’s easy to “go to definition” on the wiki link which opens the file…
  2. I wanted to track page linking… this is something core for me as I am building out my personal knowledge base, but I have key areas in my life where I want to see graphical links, or at least make it easy to trace thoughts I’ve had like clicking through wikipedia, so the find_backlinks function brings up a menu of all the pages that link to the one I’m in

I’m sure I’ll add more functions as time goes on - it’d be ncie to open certain slash pages like Now with a keymap… drop me a note at nic@pype.dev if you’ve got any great ideas!
